correctness.rationale: The Fourier transform of a positive-height simple Cauchy kernel has support on positive frequencies and the stated exponential weight; periodizing it gives a convergent geometric series on 0<omega<1. The bounded Zak multiplier is invertible exactly when it is bounded below in essential modulus; continuity on the one-sided compact strip makes even a boundary zero an obstruction. After solving for lambda, the two fractional-linear ratios have imaginary parts equal to sin(2 pi x) times r(1−q) or −rq(1−q), divided by their respective squared denominators and multiplied by 1/s or s. The ratio of squared denominators increases with cos(2 pi x), so (H) makes the summed coefficient strictly positive. The only real solutions therefore lie on x=0 or x=1/2. On the first fiber c_+/s+d_+s decreases; on the second c_-/s+d_-s has its unique interior minimum at s*=sqrt(c_-/d_-), and its greater endpoint is at q since c_-/d_->q. These are exactly the two stated closed intervals, disjoint only under the extra inequality (S). At the interior minimum the transverse imaginary derivative is nonzero and the frequency quadratic coefficient is sqrt(c_-d_-)(log q)^2, as follows also by writing the fiber as 2sqrt(c_-d_-)cosh((omega−omega*)log q). This gives two interior branches with the stated splitting. For (r,q)=(4/5,1/4), exact substitution gives (c_+,d_+,c_-,d_-)=(4,16/19,2/3,8/7), the four stated endpoints, and the stated splitting coefficient.
residual_risks: No classification outside (H), separation without (S), or quantitative stable-phase frame bounds are asserted.
